transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Maya from SE is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Nair: We're good, thanks. Excited to learn more, we chatted over email about getting started quickly.
[00:12] Jordan Park: Great. Quick agenda: understand your use case and success criteria, show how the PLG quickstart works, and identify blockers — especially around security or capacity needs.
[00:22] Samira Ortiz: That sounds good. Our main goal is to add an assistant into our product to help customers generate insights from genomic pipelines, but we need it to be fast and not too expensive per request.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Awesome, so two things I want to clarify: latency expectations and data sensitivity. Are you looking at sub-200ms for interactive use?
[00:38] Ethan Cole: For core flows, under 300ms is acceptable, under 200ms ideal. For batch jobs it's fine if it's longer. Also we can obfuscate PII but the sequence data is sens-- it's proprietary.
[00:49] Luis Moreno: From security side, we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and ideally customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). We might need VPC or Private for certain datasets.
[00:59] Jordan Park: Totally makes sense. For PLG quickstart we usually recommend starting on Redwood Hosted API — you can get free credits, it's the fastest time-to-first-token, and you can evaluate latency with our sample prompts. When you need stricter controls or sustained throughput we show Dedicated or Private options.
[01:16] Priya Nair: How long is the quickstart process? Like signing up, getting tokens, and making first call?
[01:21] Maya Singh: Typically under 10 minutes — sign up, claim free credits, create an API key, and hit our playground or curl. Time-to-first-token is usually under a minute if your infra isn't blocking outbound.
[01:31] Ethan Cole: Any gotchas with firewall / corporate proxy?
[01:34] Maya Singh: If you block outbound TLS to our endpoints you'll need to allow *.redwood.ai or the specific region endpoint. For Private deployments we can integrate inside your VPC.
[01:44] Samira Ortiz: Pricing — we need a ballpark. Is hosted per token?
[01:47] Jordan Park: Yes hosted has usage-based pricing (per-token for generation and per-embedding). We can give an estimate once we know your prompt and token counts. Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly/annual contracts, and Private has platform fees plus support.
[01:59] Priya Nair: And quality — do you run open models or your own?
[02:03] Maya Singh: We support a curated model catalog — open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. We also have tooling for quantization and batching to reduce cost. For sensitive data some customers prefer Private so models and logs stay in their network.
[02:17] Ethan Cole: For our pilot we'll start with a smaller open model, run evals, then maybe move to a higher-quality model. How easy to switch models?
[02:24] Jordan Park: Very easy — same API surface, pin model versions, and we support rollouts/canary. Also Redwood Console gives per-model dashboards.
[02:31] Luis Moreno: On encryption, do you support CMEK?
[02:34] Maya Singh: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we support KMS integration in enterprise plans. We'll share the KMS/HSM section in the security pack.
[02:45] Samira Ortiz: What's the typical time to migrate from Hosted to Dedicated?
[02:49] Jordan Park: Depends on needs — if it's about capacity and predictable throughput, often a few weeks to provision Dedicated pools. For strict network isolation (Private/VPC) it can be months depending on approvals and on-prem considerations.
[03:00] Priya Nair: Good to know. For the quickstart, can we test streaming responses and function/tool calling?
[03:06] Maya Singh: Yep, the hosted API supports streaming and structured output. Quickstart includes examples for streaming and functions.
[03:12] Ethan Cole: We're also curious about caching — we have a lot of prefix reuse in prompts.
[03:16] Maya Singh: Redwood has prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching which can dramatically lower per-token cost for repeated prompts. We'll show some configs in the docs.
[03:25] Samira Ortiz: Any mention of competitors we should be aware of?
[03:27] Jordan Park: Some customers compare to OpenAI for API simplicity, Anthropic for model quality, and folks sometimes consider self-hosted via Replicate. We emphasize production-first tooling and cost controls.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Ok, security checklist — we'll need SOC2 report, pen-test summary, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and data residency options.
[03:48] Maya Singh: We'll package that and send it. For SSO we support SAML/OIDC; RBAC is in Redwood Console, and audit logs are available with enterprise retention options.
[03:58] Luis Moreno: Also need contractual language on data processing and breach notifications.
[04:02] Jordan Park: We'll attach standard DPA and raise any specific legal asks with our contracts team.
[04:08] Samira Ortiz: Timeline? We're trying to ship an MVP in Q2, so quick turnaround on trial would help.
[04:15] Jordan Park: Sounds feasible. Quickstart trial this week, analyze metrics, then decision on Dedicated pilot by mid-April if results look good.
[04:23] Ethan Cole: For benchmarking, can Redwood run a short perf test on our sample payloads?
[04:28] Maya Singh: We can help run a bench on Hosted to validate latency and cost; for Dedicated we can provision a small test pool. We'll need your sample prompts and token estimates.
[04:38] Priya Nair: We'll share a sample dataset and a few representative prompts.
[04:42] Jordan Park: Sweet. Next steps recap: Jordan will send quickstart signup, free credits, and org invite; Maya will send SOC2/security pack and a short checklist for firewall settings; Ethan/Priya will run the quickstart and share bench notes. We'll schedule a follow-up demo for Dedicated the week of 3/16.
[04:58] Samira Ortiz: That works. Any immediate blockers?
[05:01] Luis Moreno: Just internal approvals for sharing some sample sequences; we'll follow up with legal.
[05:05] Jordan Park: Understood. We'll mark that as an open action. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the links.
[05:12] Priya Nair: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:14] Jordan Park: Thanks, bye.
questions: What's the time-to-first-token for the quickstart?
What security docs do you provide (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)?
When should we consider Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private?
